title: Constellation filter is an unsearchable list of 3-letter abbreviations
reasoning: Every part of the claim is present. _ConstellationDropdown (_filter_controls.dart:250-289) is now a _ControlChip opening _ConstellationPickerDialog: a search field, rows rendered '<Full name> (<Abbr>)' sorted by full name, a match on either spelling, a live '<n> constellations in tonight's candidates' count, and an explicit 'Any constellation' action. The null-vs-empty-string protocol is right: a barrier dismiss returns null and is a no-op, '' means clear — the classic inversion here (dismiss silently clearing the filter) is explicitly avoided at line 279. The shared table is real: constellation_names.dart holds all 88 abbreviations plus constellationFullName(), it is exported from skotiq_planetarium.dart, and catalog.dart:334 now delegates (`return constellationFullName(abbr)`) with its 88-entry private _constellationNames map deleted — I diffed the removal entry by entry, nothing was dropped. Not INCOMPLETE: the chip list is built once in _ControlsBarChips and consumed by BOTH the inline desktop Wrap (_header_and_controls_bar.dart:110) and the phone filter sheet (:182), so both surfaces get the picker. availableConstellationsProvider (suggestion_filter_provider.dart:250) does derive from the unfiltered tonight suggestion set, so the finding's 'only tonight's constellations' ask was already satisfied.
evidence: constellation_filter_picker_test.dart: 4/4 green, and it drives the real _ConstellationPickerDialog through showConstellationPickerForTest (same class instantiated by production at line 270). It pins the four things that matter: full names present, 'Constellation: And' prefix gone, typing 'ursa' narrows to Ursa Major and returns the ABBREVIATION 'UMa' (the filter still speaks what catalog rows store), 'cvn' matches by abbreviation, and 'Any constellation' returns '' not null. Two residuals, neither verdict-changing: (1) the active chip reads just 'Cygnus' with no 'Constellation:' noun, where the inactive state reads 'Constellation: any' — only the star icon says which filter it is; (2) constellationFullName() returns its input unchanged for unrecognised values, so a catalog row that already stores a full name would render 'Cygnus (Cygnus)'. Every writer I traced (Target.constellation from the library/catalog import) stores the abbreviation, and the pre-fix UI observably showed abbreviations, so this is a latent edge, not a live one. [RE-CONFIRMED this session: constellation_names.dart:102 defines constellationFullName and catalog.dart:335 still delegates to it; skotiq_planetarium 505/505 green, so the map move broke nothing on the catalog side.]

title: The Rationale block never names the target it is explaining (and calls a target with no frames a "large unfinished dataset")

I independently confirmed the arithmetic claim in target_suggestion_service._calculateDataProgress (lines 328-360): with no plan it returns 0.1 when integration > 0 and 0.0 when there is none, and with a plan it returns totalIntegrationSecs/expectedTotalSecs, which is exactly 0.0 for a target with no frames — so `> 0` excludes precisely the zero-frame case and nothing else. title: Getting a target into the scheduler is a three-deep dead end; every empty state points at another empty state
reasoning: The bulk of the claim is real and well built. project_dialogs.dart now watches installedCatalogSearchProvider(_query) (new, suggestion_filter_provider.dart:551 — genuinely different from plannerInstalledCatalogSearchProvider, which excludes tonight's candidates), lists 'Not in your targets yet' rows with type/mag/constellation, filters out anything already in the library by name OR catalogId, disables the whole list while an add is in flight (_adding), and calls the pre-existing host-aware TargetLibraryService.ensureCatalogTarget, which dedups through resolveDbTargetForCatalog. The unit claim checks out: CatalogSearchResult.ra is documented degrees in search_models.dart:6 and independently corroborated by the pre-existing planner path _search_results.dart:138, which also divides by 15. The caller does attach (projects_tab_content.dart:369-400 pops an int and calls projectService.addTarget). WHAT IS MISSING: nothing is bundled — the OpenNGC catalog is a DOWNLOAD (CatalogManager.initialize only sets a directory; getDsoCatalogStatus is a file check; there are no catalog assets in any pubspec). On the fresh profile this finding is explicitly about, the library is empty AND no catalog exists, so installedCatalogSearchProvider returns [] for every query and the new empty state says 'Search for an object by name or catalog id — M31, NGC 7000, IC 1805' and then, once the user does, 'Nothing in your library or the installed sky catalogs matches "M31"'. That is the finding's own shape — an empty state pointing at another empty state — with better copy. The app already knows how to handle this exact case one file away: _filtered_empty_state.dart:55-75 checks catalogStateProvider.dsoCatalogStatus.isInstalled and offers 'Open catalog settings'.
evidence: add_target_can_add_test.dart passes as shipped and is a good test — it drives the real ProjectsTabContent, opens the real sheet, types, taps the catalog row, and asserts BOTH that ensureCatalogTarget got raHours 10.68/15 and that ProjectService.addTarget received (project 3, target 77). But it stubs installedCatalogSearchProvider to a world where the catalog is installed, which is exactly the path that hides the gap. I confirmed the gap by construction rather than by argument: with catalogStateProvider forced to dsoInstalled:false and the search returning [], the pre-repair sheet rendered 'No targets yet / Search for an object by name or catalog id…' and, after typing M31, 'Nothing in your library or the installed sky catalogs matches "M31"' — no route out. SEVERANCE DONE on the repair: guarding the new branch with `&& DateTime.now().year < 2000` made the new test fail on 'Found 0 widgets with text "No sky catalog installed"'; restored, 2/2 green. [RE-CONFIRMED this session: the repaired branch 'No sky catalog installed' is still at project_dialogs.dart:254 and asserted twice in add_target_can_add_test.dart; no other agent has clobbered it.]

title: Scheduler moon avoidance is illumination-only; the app has moon separation everywhere else
reasoning: The capability claim is fully real and is a cause fix, not a disclosure. TargetConstraintKind.moonSeparationMin exists (target_constraint.dart:26) with moonSeparationMinDeg (:154), encodePayload writes {'min_deg':...} (:224) and fromRow reads it back (:272-279) through payload_json with no schema migration, exactly as claimed; props includes the new field so equality/copyWith are honest. The engine evaluates it in the SAME hard-constraint loop as the others (scheduler_engine.dart:834-852), reusing _moonPosition (the existing Meeus ephemeris) and _angularSeparation, and the rejection reason states the actual separation, the minimum, AND the moon's lit fraction. The wizard is wired end to end: kind card (wizard_kind_step.dart:105-114), a 0-180 slider with 180 divisions (_MoonSeparationField, constraint_fields.dart:170-206), review sentence (wizard_params_review.dart:194-198), row label 'Min moon separation' (constraint_rows.dart:91), _save building the constraint (add_constraint_wizard_dialog.dart:220-226), default 30 deg in both the wizard (:53) and the inline editor fallback (constraint_fields.dart:34). Dart's exhaustive enum switches forced every consumer to be updated, and the headless API validates kind generically off TargetConstraintKind.values (planning_data_handlers.dart:181) so /api/target-constraints accepts it with no edit. WHAT IS NOT TRUE is the last clause of the summary: 'the illumination card was renamed from the over-broad Moon avoidance to Moon illumination now that the pair exists.' The rename covered Step 1's card title and the row label but MISSED the Step 3 review headline, which still read typeLabel = 'Moon avoidance' (wizard_params_review.dart:190). That is the same wizard, three taps apart: the operator picks a card labelled 'Moon illumination', and the confirmation card they press Save under is headed 'Moon avoidance' — the exact over-broad name the fixer said they removed, and now genuinely ambiguous because a second moon constraint sits beside it in the list. Classic INCOMPLETE (one of several call sites). A second copy of the same ambiguity: target_score_row.dart:183 collapsed ANY rejection reason containing 'moon' to one 'Moon avoidance' status chip, so the scheduler's target list could not tell the operator whether a target was skipped for a bright moon (wait a few nights) or a close moon (wait a few hours) — two opposite responses behind one label. On-sky confirmation that the separation gate matches the real sky is not possible here; the ephemeris is the engine's own pre-existing Meeus code, unchanged by this fix.
evidence: TWO SEVERANCES DONE, both red. (a) Engine: guarded the moonSeparationMin case body with `if (false && minSep != null)` — moon_separation_constraint_test.dart went '+5 All tests passed' to '+3 -2', the two rejection cases failing with Expected true / Actual false, while the disabled-constraint and payload-round-trip cases stayed green (i.e. the test is bound to the production evaluation, not to a helper). Restored, 5/5. (b) UI: made _save emit moonIlluminationMax instead — target_constraints_editor_test.dart went 6/6 to '+5 -1' with 'Expected: TargetConstraintKind.moonSeparationMin / Actual: TargetConstraintKind.moonIlluminationMax'. That widget test is the good kind: it pumps the real TargetConstraintsEditor, walks the real 3-step wizard by key, saves, and reads the row back out of a real in-memory database through TargetConstraintService. Restored, 6/6. I confirmed the 'Moon avoidance' leftover by reading, not inferring: grep across the repo for the literal string found it at wizard_params_review.dart:190 and target_score_row.dart:183 (the third hit, target_scheduler_properties.dart:158, is the moon SCORE-factor toggle where 'avoidance' is still the right umbrella word, so I left it). Regressions: none — packages/skotiq_core/test/services/scheduler/ 84/84 and packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/scheduler/ 18/18 both green after the repair.
